# E045 -- Twitter External Brand Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Company:** Twitter
- **Industry:** Social Media
- **Year:** 2020
- **Source file:** twitter-external-brand-guidelines-01272021-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 16
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "Twitter Brand Guidelines" -- October 2020, external-facing
- Covers core brand elements: logo, #hashtag, @reply, and Tweets
- Intentionally kept short; not exhaustive
- Contact: trademarks@twitter.com for anything not specifically covered
- Pre-rebrand document (before X rebrand)

## Logo
- Twitter logo is always either **blue or white** -- no other colors
- On imagery: always white version; for light backgrounds, apply 10-20% black tint for legibility
- **Social icons** available in four container shapes:
  - Logo Social Icon (preferred -- logo without container)
  - Circular Social Icon
  - Square Social Icon
  - Rounded Square Social Icon
- All social icons: minimum width 32px
- Display at equal size and height to other social icons
- Background of icon container can be changed to match creative
- Preference: "Whenever possible, take our logo out of its container"

## Typography
- **Helvetica Neue Regular** -- for @handle, Tweet body, and timestamp in Tweet treatments
- **Helvetica Neue Bold** -- for username in Tweet treatments
- No broader typography system specified (external-only document)

## Color
- **Brand Blue** -- primary (specific hex not in sampled pages but historically #1DA1F2)
- **White** -- secondary logo color
- Dark mode Tweet treatments available as alternative to white

## Graphics
- Tweet treatments are a core graphic element -- specific templates for embedding real Tweets
- Tweet + Media template variant exists
- Dark mode Tweet variant available

## Photography
- Not covered in this document

## Applications
- **Tweet treatments:** real Tweets used in marketing materials
  - Must be real and exist on the platform
  - Cannot alter the message or pulled-out elements
  - Cannot editorialize or discriminate based on content
  - Must credit full name + handle + Twitter logo
  - Twitter cannot grant permission for third-party Tweets, logos, or images
  - Own Tweets can be freely used if guidelines are followed
  - Don't alter images in Tweet + Media templates

## Tone of Voice
- Casual, friendly, concise: "It shouldn't take long to read (we kept it short)"
- Helpful and approachable but legally precise when needed

## Outliers
- **Pre-X rebrand artifact** -- this is the original Twitter bird-era brand guidelines from 2020
- Only 16 pages -- one of the shortest guidelines documents encountered
- Tweet treatments section is unique -- no other social platform formalizes how their content should appear in third-party marketing to this degree
- Helvetica Neue specified only for Tweet rendering, not as a broader brand typeface
- "Take our logo out of its container" preference is unusual -- most brands prefer contained logos
- No color hex values provided in the text (relies on downloadable assets from brand page)

## Quality Score
- **2/5** -- Functional external partner guide covering logo and Tweet usage basics; very limited scope with no typography system, minimal color specification, no photography or graphics guidance; serves its narrow purpose but is not a comprehensive brand system
